record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: Let A be a Banach lattice algebra, and suppose there is a faithful algebra homomorphism from A into a space of regular operators L^r(E) that preserves finite suprema and infima. Which such algebras A admit a representation of this kind with E Dedekind complete?

evidence.quote: If there is such a representation of A in \({\mathcal L}^r(E)\) , as asked in Problem 2 , then it would be tempting to compose it with the map \(T\mapsto T^{**}:{\mathcal L}^r(E)\rightarrow {\mathcal L}^r(E^{**})\) to obtain a representation of A as a space of regular operators on a Dedekind complete Banach lattice. However, the map \(T\mapsto T^{**}\) need not be a lattice homomorphism, so this process will fail. Therefore it is a separate question to characterize those A which can be represented in this way in \({\mathcal L}^r(E)\) , with E being Dedekind complete.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a Banach lattice algebra; that is, $A$ is simultaneously a Banach algebra and a Banach lattice such that the product of two positive elements is positive, and the lattice and algebra structures are compatible with the norm. For a Banach lattice $E$, let $\mathcal{L}^r(E)$ denote the Banach lattice algebra of regular operators on $E$ (operators that can be written as the difference of two positive operators), with composition as multiplication.

Assume there exists a faithful homomorphism $\pi : A \to \mathcal{L}^r(F)$ for some Banach lattice $F$, where $\pi$ is simultaneously an algebra homomorphism and a lattice homomorphism (i.e., preserves finite suprema and infima).

Characterize those Banach lattice algebras $A$ that admit a faithful representation $\pi : A \to \mathcal{L}^r(E)$ of this kind (simultaneously an algebra homomorphism and a lattice homomorphism) where, additionally, the Banach lattice $E$ is Dedekind complete (every non-empty order-bounded subset of $E$ has a supremum).
artifact.status_search_result: A counterexample has been produced: there exist unital Banach lattice algebras of dimension 2 that admit no faithful representation (as algebra-and-lattice homomorphism) on any Dedekind complete vector lattice, showing not every Banach lattice algebra admits such a representation. However, a full characterization of those Banach lattice algebras which do admit such a Dedekind-complete representation appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Banach lattice algebras: some questions, but very few answers
status_evidence.snippet: There exist unital Banach lattice algebras of dimension 2 that admit no faithful representation on any Dedekind complete vector lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Not every Banach lattice algebra admits a faithful representation as regular operators on a Dedekind complete Banach lattice.

status_evidence.title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: It is a separate question to characterize those A which can be represented in this way in L^r(E), with E being Dedekind complete.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization problem is posed as an open question.
